g.text: Every metre of both curbs of every street used for parking:

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; fill: #1f2428

g.text: 1,376,168 to 1,651,402 vehicles (6 to 5 m each; 8,257 km of curb)

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; fill: #1f2428

g.text: Every lane of every street full, nose to tail:

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; fill: #1f2428

g.text: 787,152 to 1,049,536 vehicles (8 to 6 m each; 6,297 km of lanes at least)

g.text: Montréal's automobiles against two physical bounds of its streets

text.style: font-size: 10px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; text-anchor: start; fill: #5f6b74

g.text: Automobiles and light trucks, municipality of Montréal; the bounds are hypothetical limits, not measurements

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; fill: #5f6b74

g.text: Bounds from the City's géobase of October 14, 2026: 4,129 km of street in the municipality (autoroutes, bridges, tunnels, ramps and back lanes left out). Curb: no deduction for corners, driveways, hydrants, bus stops or

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; fill: #5f6b74

g.text: signs, so real street parking is lower. Lanes: one counted for a one-way street and two for a two-way street, since the file gives no lane count. Vehicles kept off the street are in neither bound, the registered vehicles are never

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; fill: #5f6b74

g.text: all on the road at once, and traffic stops flowing well before every lane is full.

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; fill: #5f6b74

g.text: Sources: SAAQ, open data « Véhicules en circulation », 2011–2022 (files of December 18, 2023); SAAQ, files released under the access Act, file 03.06.34729 (decision of September 17, 2025), 2023–2024.
